verdict: Tesla's revenue rose 16% to $22.4B and operating profit more than doubled to $941M off a weak year-ago quarter — but heavy AI and factory spending kept the bottom line thin at $491M.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: $3.9B of operating cash flow less $2.5B of capex

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Car sales, leasing and regulatory credits — up 16% YoY on 358,023 deliveries, though regulatory credit revenue was $380M vs $595M a year ago.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, service centers, parts and FSD (supervised-driving) subscriptions — the fastest-growing part of Tesla, up 42% YoY.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack battery systems and solar — down 12% YoY and well below the prior quarter's $3.8B, a lumpy business that swings with big project deliveries.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot, Cybercab and new vehicles — up 38% YoY as Tesla builds out its AI compute and robotaxi infrastructure.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day — up 47% YoY.

takeaways.title: Profit bounced off a weak base
takeaways.text: Operating income more than doubled from a soft year-ago quarter to $941M, and gross margin widened to 21.1% — the best in a year — helped by lower cost per vehicle and more FSD sales.

takeaways.title: Energy slipped
takeaways.text: Energy generation and storage revenue fell 12% YoY to $2.4B (and dropped from $3.8B the prior quarter) while services revenue jumped 42% — the non-car business is growing, but unevenly.

takeaways.title: A big other-expense line
takeaways.text: Below operating profit, $535M of other expense (net) plus interest costs pulled pre-tax profit down to $748M, leaving net income of $491M — a 2.2% margin on $22.4B of revenue.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $1,030M (vs $573M a year ago), swollen by the 2025 CEO Performance Award — a non-cash cost inside operating expenses. Non-GAAP net income was $1,453M ($0.41 a share) vs GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders of $477M ($0.13).
otherDetail: Interest income of $434M, less $92M of interest expense and $535M of other expense, net — a net −$193M below operating profit.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $491M; $477M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).
